walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordinate Geometry — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordinate Geometry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordinate Geometry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11) is:
Which line is perpendicular to y = 2x + 1?
What is the relationship between the angle at the centre and the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc?
options: The angles are equal because they are subtended by the same arc.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
It reaches 0 at the millionth term.
The angle at the centre is half the angle at the circumference.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
options: It reaches 0 at the millionth term.
Simple interest is calculated only on the original amount; compound interest is calculated on the original amount plus accumulated interest.
Simple interest grows faster than compound because it has fewer steps.
Simple and compound interest give the same total — compound just uses a different formula.
Simple interest grows faster than compound because it has fewer steps.
No — it approaches 0 as the limit but no term is ever exactly 0.
It reaches 0 at the millionth term.
Eventually a term will be so small it equals 0.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Gradient of a line”?
options: (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r² gives circle with centre (a, b) and radius r.
m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). Positive m: upward slope; negative m: downward; m = 0: horizontal.
d = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]. Pythagoras applied to the coordinate plane.
Radius at point of tangency is perpendicular to tangent. Useful for finding tangent equation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Perpendicular lines”?
options: If two lines have gradients m₁ and m₂, they are perpendicular ⟺ m₁m₂ = −1.
d = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]. Pythagoras applied to the coordinate plane.
y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) or y = mx + c. Useful forms for different given data.
m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). Positive m: upward slope; negative m: downward; m = 0: horizontal.
